name: Communalism
summary: Communalism, as Murray Bookchin formulated it, holds that society should be run by face-to-face popular assemblies in municipalities that confederate through mandated, recallable delegates. It seeks to replace the nation-state, capitalism and all social hierarchy with a municipalized, ecological economy that is neither privately owned nor nationalized.
scope: Murray Bookchin's Communalism (libertarian municipalism, post-1999), drawn from The Communalist Project and Libertarian Municipalism: An Overview, and its adoption by Abdullah Ocalan as democratic confederalism. It excludes the unrelated South Asian communalism meaning sectarian religious identity politics.

sources.usedFor: Overview, municipalization versus nationalization, and the Rojava link.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed directly; a municipalized economy would provide basic services as public goods, but via municipal confederations rather than the national government.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Communalism aims to abolish wage-and-profit relations by municipalizing the economy, so a wage-floor reform is neither a core demand nor rejected as such.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Bookchin says Communalists should discredit and ultimately efface the market system, whose grow-or-die logic he blames for the ecological crisis.

public-ownership.rationale: He rejects nationalization as bureaucratic centralization but wants key enterprises under municipal assembly control, so public ownership yes, state ownership no.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a Communalist theme; the program targets the property system itself rather than redistribution through national taxation.

unions-good.rationale: He criticizes syndicalism for factory-centred economic determinism and wants workers to act as citizens, though he does not oppose workers organizing.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bookchin rejects private ownership of the means of production, holding that basic community resources should not be privately owned.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Communalism seeks to replace corporations by municipal control and not to regulate them within capitalism, which he sees as impervious to reform.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; his rejection of market logic and emphasis on solidarity suggest opposition, though he is no defender of the state welfare apparatus.

worker-ownership.rationale: Bookchin warns that self-managed firms drift into competing collective capitalism and wants enterprises under municipal assembly control instead.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; he treats the state apparatus as alien to human development and would distrust state surveillance, inferred from his anti-statism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; as a libertarian socialist heir to the New Left he is likely tolerant, but this is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; assemblies would uphold civil rights, but no source speaks on legally restricting speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Bookchin demands direct democracy in popular assemblies with mandated, recallable delegates, and sees concentrated power as the problem.

state-harmful.rationale: He calls the state an alien formation and a thorn in human development, though he wants a municipal public sphere with coordinating confederal institutions.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no stated position.

empower-police-military.rationale: He lists police and the military as part of the coercive state apparatus that the municipal confederation is meant to replace.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not documented as holding a common view.

decide-locally.rationale: The central claim is that politics belongs in face-to-face municipal assemblies, with only coordinative confederal functions above them.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his social ecology view that social conditions and hierarchy cause social problems.

traditional-family.rationale: He names patricentric hierarchy as a historical form of domination, so he would not treat traditional family structure as a foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the opposition to hierarchy and domination and the New Left lineage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from his anti-patriarchal social ecology and left-libertarian tradition.

more-religion-public.rationale: Bookchin was an atheist who held that spirituality should be naturalistic and free of mystical regressions, though tolerant of belief.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed directly; he opposes all hierarchy and domination, but also criticizes identity-based politics that fractures radical movements.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He describes patricentricity as a historical development, not a fixed natural order, implying gender roles are socially produced.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He criticizes nationalism and cautions that self-managed communities may become parochial, even racist, if they celebrate separate identity.

gradual-change.rationale: He seeks a dual power in which free municipalities confront the nation-state and transitional demands that open revolutionary change, not respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He warns that parochial communities risk becoming racist and favours a universal citizenship, so would oppose restriction, inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He wants power moved down to municipal confederations, away from nation-states, and no source endorses supranational bodies like the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade extends the grow-or-die market that he wants to efface; he favours municipal, human-scale economies.

nation-first.rationale: He sees nationalism as having led workers to fight for their rulers and wants confederal solidarity rather than national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; no source states a position.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed directly; the ideal of universal citizenship and opposition to nationalism suggests sympathy, but borders are not discussed.

limit-growth.rationale: He argues capitalism's grow-or-die imperative conflicts with ecology's imperative of interdependence and limit.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He sees the ecological crisis as arising from capitalism, but demands action through municipal confederation rather than national government.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He rejects technological fixes alone, favouring ecotechnologies within a changed social order that removes domination.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; his preference for decentralized renewables suggests opposition, inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: He builds dual power toward revolutionary change and says a Communalist society cannot simply be legislated into existence.

experts-over-public.rationale: He wants policy made by the citizens in assemblies and opposes representatives preempting the citizen's right to shape policy.

central-planning.rationale: He rejects nationalization and centralized bureaucracy, and wants the economy municipalized under local assemblies.

socialized-markets.rationale: He warns that self-managed enterprises drift into collective capitalism and wants the market system effaced, even if firms are collectively owned.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; a tax-based reform within the market would not fit his call to municipalize land and enterprises.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a state income scheme clashes with his anti-statism but fits his solidarity ethic.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; national protectionism conflicts with his preference for municipal control over national policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He criticizes nationalization as producing a privatized economy in collectivized form and wants economic decisions in local assemblies.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He rejects private ownership of means of production in favour of municipal custody, though small property is not his main target.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He wants profit-driven economics replaced by ethics and solidarity, but sources do not specify abolishing money and wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; he opposes both market and state control of the economy and nothing is said of money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He criticizes syndicalist occupational interest groups and wants citizens to decide as citizens, not as employers or workers bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: He rejects Bolshevik authoritarianism and denounces parliamentary opportunism, favouring directly democratic assemblies.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hierarchy is the basic problem he wants overcome, and he demands directly democratic popular assemblies.

democracy-best.rationale: He champions direct democracy, but he contrasts it with the republican institutions of existing democracies, which he distrusts.

direct-votes.rationale: Communalist politics is the formulation of policy by directly democratic popular assemblies, with citizens deciding in face-to-face assembly.

workers-councils.rationale: He rejects workers' control and syndicalism in favour of municipal assemblies of citizens, so councils of workers are not the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: He says confederates may withdraw only with the whole confederation's approval, while favouring municipal autonomy, so this is split.

natural-rulers.rationale: He opposes hierarchy as such and argues that domination is socially produced rather than natural.

political-violence-never.rationale: He does not explicitly endorse or reject violence, but supports revolutionary dual power and forceful correction of abuses.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; his social ecology of solidarity and anti-nationalism suggests rejection, inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: He sees politics as a secular public sphere of citizens and favours naturalistic spirituality, though religion itself is not suppressed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He holds that policy is formulated by popular assemblies, and favours a naturalism free of supernatural claims.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private courts and defence is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's opposition to market logic and private economic power (s1).

military-superiority.rationale: He lists the military among state apparatus to be replaced by confederation and opposes nationalist power projection.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He warns against parochial, even racist, communities and favours a citizenship that transcends identity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He draws on Marx but argues hierarchy is distinct from class, and sees domination as broader than class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed directly; his ideal of solidarity and need-based ethics implies sympathy but he does not frame it so.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; local self-governance and early usufruct customs suggest sympathy, but the sources are silent.

civilizational-union.rationale: He opposes the nation-state and nationalism but wants confederation through municipalities, not civilizational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He argues that capitalism is structurally amoral and that a Communalist society would replace material gain with human solidarity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He stresses citizenship and civic education, but invokes civil and human rights as the basis of confederal authority.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: His ethics of complementarity has humans support natural processes, though he rejects pantheist or mystical views of nature.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He blames capitalism's growth logic rather than industrial technology as such, and favours human-scaled ecotechnologies.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He rejects technology-centred fixes and favours human-scale, durable production; no source speaks to accelerating change.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Policy belongs to citizens in face-to-face assemblies, so delegating government decisions to algorithms contradicts the core.

restore-past-order.rationale: He seeks a new ecological society, though he draws on past traditions of commons and assemblies and opposes the reactionary nostalgia he criticizes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He treats ethics and social theory as the guide to action, and criticizes eclecticism and relativism.

direct-action.rationale: He insists Communalists run in municipal elections to win assemblies, though opposing parliamentary candidacies, and criticizes small-group direct action as lifestyle politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: He builds the new society within the shell of the old through assemblies and dual power, so means anticipate ends, but he does not state this principle so.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He wants an ecotechnological, rational society with human-scale industry, not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He favours craftsmanship and human-scale production but sources do not call for abolishing the division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He holds that ethics and solidarity should replace material gain and early usufruct customs support distribution by community need.

production-for-use.rationale: He wants human-centred production replacing capitalism's profit-driven grow-or-die logic, with the economy placed under the community.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He criticizes profit-driven private ownership as exploiting people, though he stresses hierarchy and domination beyond class exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejects Bolshevik authoritarianism and says class conflict plays out in popular assemblies, not under proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; land would be under municipal custody but farming organization is not specified.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He notes nationalism led workers to fight in WWI but does not argue that capitalism inevitably causes imperialist war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; he holds common resources belong to the community, so taxation as theft conflicts with his premises.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; he accepts majority decisions by assemblies bound by civil rights, which goes beyond a pure harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He criticizes individualism in anarchism and argues freedom is social, found in the public sphere of citizens.

conscription.rationale: He treats the military as part of the state apparatus; no source speaks on conscription, so inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: He holds that freedom is exercised through participation in assemblies, not exit, and criticizes the personal-liberty orientation.

state-as-business.rationale: He sees capitalism's market logic as the root of ecological harm and wants politics as citizen self-management, not business-like governance.

positive-liberty.rationale: He distinguishes social freedom from personal liberty and argues freedom takes institutional form in public assemblies.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He opposes racism and holds that domination is socially produced, not natural.

organic-representation.rationale: He opposes representation by occupational interest groups and wants citizens in assemblies with mandated, recallable delegates.

total-state.rationale: He calls the state alien and a thorn in human development and wants power moved to municipalities.

national-rebirth.rationale: He criticizes nationalism and favours a rational, universalist, ecological society.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposes nationalism and the nation-state, favouring confederation of municipalities.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He opposes hierarchy and favours accountable, recallable delegates in place of personal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: He opposes domination in all forms and wants production placed under community assemblies.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He criticizes postmodernist relativism and eclecticism and defends reason within social ecology.

universal-morality.rationale: He rejects relativism and builds an ethics of complementarity grounded in naturalism, which he treats as rational.

single-common-good.rationale: He wants citizens to consider the general interest rather than particular identities, which comes near a common good, though it is decided by majority vote.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; he opposes the nation-state in principle.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He rejects workers' control of firms as syndicalist economic determinism and wants municipal assemblies of citizens to decide.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; market mechanisms in education conflict with his rejection of markets.

economic-freedom.rationale: He criticizes market freedom as driving ecological harm and holds that freedom is political and social, found in assemblies.

rule-by-example.rationale: He wants rule by formal structures, mandate and recall of delegates, not reliance on rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: He opposes the nation-state and nationalism, favouring municipal self-determination within confederations.

force-without-un.rationale: He opposes national power politics and the nation-state, but no source speaks to force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He defends reason against postmodern relativism and wants a natural spirituality free of mystical regressions, but includes ethics.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He favours a universal citizenship ethos and warns of parochialism; no direct statement on welfare for immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; his solidarity-based ethics make conditional welfare alien, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: He wants class conflict played out in assemblies and eliminated, not partnership between employers and workers inside the market system.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; he values craftsmanship and civic education, so sacrificing cultural institutions conflicts with this.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; he is anti-nationalist but sources are silent on this bloc strategy.

workers-nation.rationale: He notes that nationalism led workers to fight for their rulers and wants a universalist citizenship.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He sees patricentricity as a form of hierarchy to be overcome.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He warns that parochial communities risk becoming racist and opposes all hierarchy and domination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He sees the state as an alien formation and hierarchy as distinct from class, so does not reduce the state to a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He favours renewable ecotechnologies and holds that capitalist growth drives ecological crisis.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; his anti-nationalism and view of citizenship as civic participation suggest opposing cultural assimilation demands.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; a conspiracy claim of this kind has no basis in his social ecology.

proportional-representation.rationale: He rejects party-based representative government in favour of direct assemblies, though would prefer PR to winner-takes-all, inferred.

national-mission.rationale: He rejects nationalism and the nation-state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He names patricentricity as a historical hierarchy and a root social problem alongside gerontocracy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He holds that political power has been absorbed by the state and that republican institutions have preempted citizens, inferred as distrust of elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: He opposes domination and coercive hierarchy and values civil and human rights as the basis for confederal authority.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not directly addressed; his demand for accountability of delegates and civil rights standards suggests agreement.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He rejects the state in favour of municipal assemblies and rejects private property in the means of production.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He warns of racist parochial communities and opposes all domination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He invokes civil and human rights as the basis of confederal standards, and opposes hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; he wants confederation and dual power but does not discuss this Marxist-Leninist debate.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; he wants local decisions within confederal civil-rights standards.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He was tolerant of religious views and defends civil rights, so legal restriction is inferred as rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; local assemblies would decide, and he does not tie law to religious practice.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; his secular naturalism and civic-education emphasis suggest agreement, inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: He rejects Bolshevik authoritarianism and wants state power replaced by popular power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He wants politics as citizens directly governing through assemblies, which is democratic consent, though he rejects liberal-representative forms.

trade-surplus.rationale: He rejects market growth and favours local human-scale production, so export-oriented mercantilism is alien, inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: He opposes racism and domination and invokes civil and human rights.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He accepts majority rule binding minorities, and says abuses would be corrected forcefully if unavoidable, so does not hold force-initiation absolutely wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He rejects capitalist competition and grow-or-die logic, favouring solidarity and complementarity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; he is anti-statist but upholds civil rights and strongly opposes racists, so split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: His social ecology centres on ending hierarchy and domination, treating freedom as the absence of domination in the public sphere.

separated-powers.rationale: He rejects republican institutions in favour of direct assembly power with confederal delegates as coordinators, not checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: He rejects Bolshevik authoritarianism and wants popular assemblies, and believes the working class itself is no longer the sole agent.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not directly stated; solidarity over material gain and need-based ethics imply it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; individual property acquisition cuts against municipal custody, inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; he opposes state coercion but is critical of syndicalism, so mildly opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He blames social hierarchy and capitalism for social and ecological problems, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He sees racism and parochialism as dangers, not diversity, and wants a universal citizenship built through participation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; he favours mandated recallable delegates chosen by assemblies, not sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He grounds confederal authority on civil and human rights and opposes state coercion.

party-controls-media.rationale: He rejects Bolshevik authoritarianism and wants popular power and a free public sphere.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's rejection of party rule and Leninism (s1).

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; his universalist citizenship ideal suggests opposition, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not directly addressed; his mandated, recallable delegates with coordinative functions only fit with no privilege.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He demands mandated delegates bound to assembly decisions, but opposes parliamentary party politics, so split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He wants confederation of municipalities with only administrative functions, but opposes nation-state unions such as the EU, inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He opposes concentrated executive power and military apparatus.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchy is his central target, so hierarchical church government is rejected, inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: He opposes hierarchy and supports popular assemblies, with naturalistic spirituality.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He notes workers fought for national rulers in WWI as a failure of nationalism, but never states a defeatist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; he defends civil rights and opposes state coercion, inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He wants delegates mandated and recallable, with rotating, accountable administrative roles.

recall-officials.rationale: He calls for full accountability of confederal delegates, with the right to recall them and firmly mandated representation.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; he opposes nation-state power politics, so ending military alliances is inferred as agreeable.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; he prefers municipal custody of land and housing over individual ownership, so mandatory home ownership does not fit.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; he criticizes the military as state apparatus, but no source on citizen militias.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He favours humanly scaled cities and municipalities as the arena of politics and not rural romanticism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He opposes nationalism, so national reunification claims are not part of his programme.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: He values civic education and reasoned participation, though criticizes the lifestyle left and postmodernists.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He rejects relativism but also celebrates diversity within a universal humanity, so split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; opposition inferred from his anti-statist and humanist stance.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his critique of patriarchal hierarchy and support for civic education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: He grounds social ecology in naturalism and evolutionary reasoning and rejects supernatural claims.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: He wants citizenship defined by participation in public affairs, not ancestry, and fears racist parochialism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with his support for cultural diversity within a universal citizenship.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; he is tolerant of religion yet holds majority decisions bind minorities, so split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He criticizes lifestyle anarchism for prizing personal liberty over social freedom, though not individuality as such.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with his anti-capitalist and solidarity ethics, inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He ties freedom to replacing capitalist and state economic structures, so political change alone is insufficient; independence itself is not discussed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed directly; a directly democratic assembly rewriting the framework suits his assembly politics, though he distrusts national institutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He rejects growth as an imperative and defends direct democracy as the form of freedom.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity ethics suggest agreement, though state-to-state aid is not his framework.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He treats the military as part of state apparatus to be replaced and rejects nationalism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He rejects concentrated executive power and favours direct assemblies, so a strong elected president is not his model.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; market-oriented monetary technocracy conflicts with assembly control, inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He opposes nationalism, so historic homeland claims do not carry weight, inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He holds that resources needed by the community should not be private and wants the economy placed under municipal custody.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He rejects nationalization as a privatized economy in collectivized form and criticizes Bolshevik authoritarianism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed explicitly; his demand for ecological standards and limits implies caution about environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: He rejects nationalism and state military blocs, inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He rejects state apparatus and favours tolerance of religion, so state subordination of the clergy does not fit.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He has no place for heads of state; politics rests in assemblies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He opposes the nation-state apparatus and favours local autonomy, though confederal withdrawal needs consent.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred head of state is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's atheism and rejection of hierarchy (s1).

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; opposition inferred from rejection of market-centred economics.

character-from-environment.rationale: He holds that domination and hierarchy are socially constructed and that social change reshapes people, citizens made by participation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He demands accountable delegates bound by formal structures and recall.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; his ecological limits and human-scale emphasis make it a low priority.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He rejects republican institutions and rule by the few.

leader-cult.rationale: He opposes hierarchy and demands formal structures and recall for any leaders.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed; he holds class conflict to be played out in assemblies and eventually eliminated.

land-redistribution.rationale: He wants land under municipal custody, not redistributed to individual farmers, so neither clearly agrees nor rejects.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; civil and human rights framework suggests agreement.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He opposes nationalism and the nation-state.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He defends civil rights and is hostile to supernaturally grounded authority, though tolerant of belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: He opposes patriarchal domination and coercive state apparatus.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; supranational monetary union runs against his municipal confederal localism.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He opposes ethnic and nationalist politics and fears racist parochialism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; municipal self-government is central but organization by nationality is not.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He criticizes Marxist economism and treats hierarchy and domination, not only economic production, as a driver.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; reforming capitalism through antitrust is not his programme, since he wants to efface the market.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He accepts majority decisions in assemblies but holds confederal civil rights standards limit them, so split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He favours municipal self-reliance but not colonial blocs, so only partial fit.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: He wants confederal ecological and civil-rights standards but opposes market-extending trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: He wants economics replaced by ethics, with solidarity displacing material gain.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He emphasizes building dual power through assemblies and municipal elections, not armed vanguard action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolition of hierarchy and domination is his core aim.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He favours universal citizenship and is wary of parochialism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He opposes domination and hierarchy among peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: He opposes nationalism, though he wants lifelong civic education in participation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He argues that capitalism's grow-or-die logic is impervious to moral appeals and drives ecological crisis.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He opposes nationalism and power projection by nation-states.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; he favours municipal self-reliance, but not as a state strategy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He opposes racism and wants assemblies bound by civil rights.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He invokes civil rights as the basis of confederal authority but rejects constitutional republican institutions, so split.

elective-rulers.rationale: He rejects rulers altogether, wanting accountable delegates and assemblies, so the statement misfits.

minority-veto.rationale: He rejects consensus and favours majority voting that binds minorities while protecting their rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed directly; consistent with his dual power opposition to state authority.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He rejects parliamentary politics and republican institutions in favour of direct assemblies.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed directly; his ecology and ethic of complementarity suggest agreement.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He rejects hierarchy and the paternalism of privileged classes, wanting self-governing citizens.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He holds that politics, as citizens managing their community, is the realm of freedom and requires lifelong participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He criticizes consumer society and capitalism's co-optation, though sources do not state it directly.

native-born-offices.rationale: He rejects nationalism and wants universal citizenship.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to a non-Leninist movement.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He opposes nationalism and nation-state claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; universal citizenship and anti-hierarchy suggest opposition to group-based leadership.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He rejects Bolshevik authoritarianism but does not equate it with fascism in the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; his opposition to domination implies rejection.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He favours universal directly democratic forms and rejects relativism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He lists the military among state apparatus to be replaced.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; he wants delegates mandated by assemblies, not a bureaucratic civil service.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with his anti-patriarchal stance.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Bookchin requires confederal delegates to be firmly mandated and recallable, accountable to the assemblies that sent them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Market-based private accounts contradict his demand to efface the market and use solidarity.

land-use-tenure.rationale: He proposes municipal custody of land and enterprises, held by the community, citing early customs of non-private basic resources.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He rejects parliamentary politics in favour of assemblies, though budget control by representatives is not addressed.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed; his tolerance of diversity suggests opposition, inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He argues capitalism's grow-or-die logic fosters consumption, and wants solidarity to replace material gain.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He opposes nation-state power politics, inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He rejects nation-state domination and nationalism.

corporate-influence.rationale: He criticizes capitalism's amorality and green capitalism's co-optation of ecological concern.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; opposes state direction and growth ideology.

residents-only-property.rationale: Municipal control of land fits, but sources do not discuss residency limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; he wants to abolish capital-wage relations, but guaranteed jobs are not discussed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He treats the nation-state as illegitimate but wants binding majority decisions within assemblies, so split.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; he rejects nation-state power but also supports civil rights standards.

industrial-unions.rationale: He criticizes syndicalism's factory focus and does not take a stance on union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He opposes racism and parochial hatreds.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; open public sphere in assemblies suggests agreement.

local-production.rationale: He favours human-scale industry and municipal control of the economy, with an emphasis on local self-reliance.

informal-organisation.rationale: He criticizes small-group informal organisation (grupismo) as a lifestyle substitute for mass action and wants formal structures.

religious-nation.rationale: He rejects nationalism and favours secular universal citizenship.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He favours municipal autonomy but confederal solidarity, so split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not directly stated, but he rejects private ownership only of productive property, not personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: He rejects Bolshevism but also capitalism and Cold War nationalism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He wants economy under municipal control and effacing markets.

religion-illusion.rationale: He was an atheist but tolerant of religion and is critical of mysticism, not a statement he develops.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He draws on Marx and acknowledges capitalism's historical dynamism, while arguing it now threatens the biosphere.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He treats hierarchy as distinct from class, so women's liberation requires ending patricentric hierarchy beyond economics.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; opposed as nationalism, inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: He calls for self-governing municipal communities that hold their economy in common, confederated.

majority-settlement.rationale: He opposes racism and nationalist domination.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejects capitalism, Bolshevik communism and nationalization, proposing communalism as a third alternative.

historical-land-claim.rationale: He rejects nationalism, so claims based on ethnic ties carry no weight.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He opposes racism and defends reason against relativism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He opposes hierarchy, domination and state coercion over personal life.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He demands direct democracy and rejects authoritarian rule.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He was an atheist and defends civil rights.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial rule is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's opposition to domination and the nation-state (s1).

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He opposes religious hierarchy and supports secular assemblies.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He defines politics as the formulation of policy by directly democratic popular assemblies of citizens.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: He treats hierarchy, patriarchy and class as interlinked forms of domination, though he criticizes identity politics.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-hierarchy and left-libertarian lineage.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He criticizes eclecticism and positions himself firmly within the left libertarian tradition.

alienated-labor.rationale: He draws on Marx's project but does not stress alienation in the sources, though he criticizes capitalism's treatment of work.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He opposes racism and parochialism, inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Divine authority is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's atheism and his location of authority in citizen assemblies (s1).

social-market-economy.rationale: He holds that capitalism cannot be reformed and the market system should be effaced.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He lists the military among state apparatus to be replaced, though a municipal defence is not detailed.

rich-first.rationale: He opposes capitalist growth and inequality.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to nation-state power politics suggests it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's rejection of hierarchy and demand for accountable delegates (s1).

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; mutualist credit is an anarchist idea he does not take up.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with anti-capitalist solidarity.

property-franchise.rationale: Property qualifications for voting is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bookchin's assemblies open to all citizens (s1).

domination-women-nature.rationale: He argues domination of nature stems from human domination, naming patriarchy among forms of hierarchy that must end together.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He criticizes capitalism's co-optation but does not discuss the press.

racial-franchise.rationale: He wants citizenship open to all, and opposes racism.

online-participation.rationale: He insists on face-to-face assemblies, so online participation is not endorsed.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with open public sphere.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: He defends civil rights and opposes hierarchical coercion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: He opposes racism and parochial hatreds.

citizens-assembly.rationale: He wants decision-making assemblies of all citizens, not randomly selected groups, so partially fits.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He sees capitalism and hierarchy as threats to freedom, though he frames it as system rather than concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; he opposes the military in general.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He was an atheist but tolerant, and opposes state coercion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He lists police as state apparatus but sources do not describe abolition of prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He favours majority voting in assemblies with minority rights protected, not communal power-sharing, inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He opposes both state and market and favours solidarity in municipal institutions, not charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; rotation of mandated delegates is consistent.

vote-delegation.rationale: He demands face-to-face assemblies and mandated delegates, not liquid delegation.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with his anti-patriarchal position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with anti-patriarchal stance.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; municipal citizenship defined by participation suggests agreement.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Bookchin's rejection of market and property relations in favour of communal control of resources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to the nation-state, militarism and hierarchy; drilled national-service movements are alien to assembly-based citizenship.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from his ecological anti-statism and rejection of the state's military apparatus.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from his opposition to state power and empire in favour of confederated municipalities.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; Communalists oppose genocide but are sceptical of formal state declarations, so the answer is inferred as neutral.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Bookchin rejects private ownership of the means of production and wants the economy municipalized, so ownership should not confer income; his emphasis is on need and community rather than a work-reward rule.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Bookchin criticized pacifism, and the Rojava application of Communalism rests on armed popular self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Communalism aims to replace the nation-state and national identity with confederated, civic municipalities, so essentialist national continuity is rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by Bookchin; he stresses social hierarchy over nature but gives no position on the sex-gender distinction.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are not documented as taking a side in this feminist debate.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Bookchin's texts do not address it, and the Rojava movement honours its fallen while rejecting nationalism, so adherents are inferred as split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from his rationalist, secular social ecology, which grounds politics in assemblies and institutions rather than a metaphysical contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as neutral because Communalism rejects national homelands as state projects but takes no stance on diaspora culture.

culture-before-state.rationale: Bookchin stresses ethical and educational renewal alongside building popular institutions, and wants the state abolished rather than built, so this is inferred as split.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his secular opposition to all hierarchy, which extends to patriarchal religious imagery.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; Communalism is secular and takes no position on judging religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Communalism opposes ethnic or hierarchical domination and puts the economy under all citizens' municipal assemblies, with minority rights protected.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its civic, multi-ethnic confederal model as applied in Rojava, which organizes by municipality rather than by merging regions for one people.

independent-unions.rationale: Communalism wants workers organised in democratic bodies answerable to their members and has no role for state-run unions; Bookchin's own focus is the municipal assembly, so this is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Communalism locates power in citizens' assemblies, not in a state acting for workers, so a society run from above is not communal; inferred, as it speaks of citizens rather than the working class.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The communalist economy is municipalised: land, utilities and services are held by the community and run through its assemblies.

second-chamber.rationale: Communalism replaces parliaments with assemblies and confederal councils rather than adding a chamber to a legislature; it does not discuss bicameralism, so this is inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Bookchin's central economic proposal is that property be municipalised, neither private nor nationalised.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal councils are made up of mandated, recallable delegates who coordinate and administer while policy stays with the local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Wage levels and the family wage are not addressed; a moneyless-minded municipal economy makes the question mostly moot.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Social ecology favours precaution and distrusts technocratic, profit-driven technology; inferred, not discussed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Bookchin favoured liberatory technology but never addressed life-extension research or its public funding.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anti-statist and decentralist, so adherents would likely welcome payments the state cannot control; inferred, though the municipal economy is not market-based.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anti-statist adherents would likely defend pseudonymous participation; inferred from the opposition to state power, not discussed.

person-over-state.rationale: Communalism aims at individual freedom realised through direct democracy, but it also makes the assembly the decision-maker; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Bookchin was a secular naturalist who criticised mysticism, though he held a rich ethics of nature; a materialist-leaning stance is inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Power flows upward from municipal assemblies; a national legislature holding revocable authority over regions is the statist order communalism rejects.

gm-crops.rationale: Social ecology is wary of biotechnology under capitalism and favours ecological, small-scale agriculture; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Bookchin criticised the megacity and 'urbanisation without cities' and wanted human-scale, decentralised municipalities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Communalism is universalist and rejects hierarchy and domination, including racial; politics is organised by citizenship in the assembly.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its universalist, anti-hierarchical outlook; not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anti-militarist and anti-imperial, with the confederalist armed forces in its Kurdish adoption framed as self-defence; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Bookchin rejects the nation-state and nationalism in favour of confederated municipalities; a nation defined by language is not a political basis he accepts (Ocalan's confederalism likewise rejects nation-state building).

communal-electorates.rationale: Communalism rests on citizen assemblies open to all residents of a municipality, which is incompatible with separate religious electorates, though it is not discussed in these terms.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: communalists oppose the nation-state itself and so do not defend its territorial integrity against partition claims.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed directly; a municipalized economy would treat education as a public good, inferred from its rejection of market provision.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Social ecology holds that capitalism's growth imperative causes ecological harm and calls for a moral economy, not pricing mechanisms within the market.

future-generations.rationale: Ecological stewardship and a rational, sustainable society are core to Bookchin's social ecology, which the Communalist Project is built on.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Bookchin opposed essentialist views of gendered nature and stressed social hierarchy as the cause, inferred from his critique of such positions.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred from opposition to the state and its standing armies, though communalists favour popular militias.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to open face-to-face assemblies and public decision-making, with no explicit statement on treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Communalists seek to replace states and the global capitalist economy, but have no program of state border controls on capital; split or indifferent.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Bookchin opposes the nation-state and its professional army and police, favouring a popular militia answerable to confederated assemblies.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Opposition to the nation-state implies rejecting inter-state wars, though Communalists accept armed defence of free municipalities; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Bookchin was critical of syndicalism and unions as a base for change, favouring municipal assemblies; inferred as split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not discussed; national-state transfers cut against municipalised economy and local control. Inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not discussed; assemblies are meant to control the economy democratically, which legal limits imposed from above would constrain. Inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; a confederal alternative to capitalism rather than reform of international rules. Inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Communalism seeks to replace the nation-state with confederated assemblies, building dual power against it rather than taking it over.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Bookchin's municipalised economy is a defined project, but decisions rest with local assemblies; inferred as split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Social ecology opposes treating nature as a commodity under the grow-or-die market; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Bookchin rejects the nation-state and nationalism in favour of municipal confederation and universal citizenship.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not discussed; hostility to capitalist debt suggests support, though not via the national state. Inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Critique of centralised state power over towns makes this plausible; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Social ecology holds a rational, cooperative potential in humanity, but Bookchin stresses historical development; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Not discussed; assemblies would run media locally, outside both state and market, so national public media is not clearly endorsed. Inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Bookchin was a rationalist critic of mysticism and hierarchy, so a perennialist claim is not part of the project; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: A municipalized, cooperative economy would give farmers community-backed credit and security, though not national price floors; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Communalism seeks to replace the nation-state and holds an ecological, anti-militarist ethic, so retaining state nuclear arms is rejected; inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Bookchin rejected class-based parties and took the municipal assembly, not a workers' party, as the vehicle of change; inferred from his case for libertarian municipalism.

ban-fgm.rationale: Opposing all social hierarchy, including patriarchy, favours a ban, though enforcement would be by communities; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equality of women is central to the rejection of domination, and Ocalan's democratic confederalism makes women's liberation a pillar; inferred from the scope.

one-language-many-names.rationale: No stated view on language classification; neutral inference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental harm is dealt with through democratic municipal decisions and an ecological economy, not private lawsuits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs are a hierarchy, and lawmaking belongs to citizens' assemblies; inferred from the anti-hierarchy core.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Social ecology puts ecological sustainability at the centre, with citizens in assemblies deciding limits on freedoms that damage it; inferred, as liberty is also prized.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Bookchin opposed hierarchical, state-driven punishment in favour of community-based justice, so fixed sentences are unlikely to be backed; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Confederal municipalism is inclusive and opposes state coercion, so a legal requirement is rejected, though learning is encouraged; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Bookchin's assembly politics centres on the municipality, not the workplace, so no stated view on dues; inferred as split.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from open face-to-face assemblies in which all residents take part; entry barriers to participation sit badly with that.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the state and of hierarchy, with minority rights protected in confederal assemblies.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Communalism rejects representative statecraft and defines democracy as direct popular rule in assemblies, so elections alone do not suffice.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to hierarchy and domination, which extends to patriarchal control over women.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to open public communication and to limiting centralised state power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from its municipalised economy of provision by need, which replaces separate welfare machinery and cash transfers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Assemblies open to all citizens and the opposition to hierarchy imply equal political rights for women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Bookchin opposes all hierarchy, patriarchy and religious hierarchy included, but gives no stated view on religion as a main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from social ecology's view that hierarchy and domination are social products, not natural facts.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of the state; equality is meant to come from the assemblies, not from state agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Bookchin treats the economy as municipalized, owned neither privately nor by the state, so a private first-claim title to land or resources is inferred to be rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Bookchin's anti-hierarchical ethics, though his rejection of the nation-state makes the answer tentative.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not discussed in these texts; Bookchin's rationalist, secular social ecology and hostility to hierarchy imply rejection of literalist scripture, inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's opposition to all social hierarchy; democratic confederalism as adopted by Ocalan puts gender equality in its institutions.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Communalism rejects both the state and nationalisation in favour of a municipalised economy, so it would not defend a bureaucratically ruled planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: The confederal model has municipal assemblies send mandated, recallable delegates to higher confederal councils, which matches indirect filling of higher offices.

national-church-status.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from opposition to the state and to hierarchy, which rules out legal privilege for a church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from commitment to local self-government and confederation; communalism opposes the nation-state rather than endorsing ethnic territories.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its stress on popular, face-to-face decision-making by the people concerned; it is not discussed directly.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the nation-state and of centralised borders, which makes colonial frontiers not worth preserving as such.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's social ecology, which favours ecological, human-scale living, though he criticised lifestyle retreat from politics.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred principles of local self-rule and ecological ethics point in different directions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not discussed; Bookchin favoured popular militias under municipal control rather than state conscription, so no clear answer.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's rejection of the nation-state and nationalism; he rooted community in municipal assemblies and ecology, not ancestral land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Bookchin's rights-based, face-to-face democracy and rejection of the coercive state are incompatible with killing suspects without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: it opposes both the nation-state system and great-power blocs, so it has no preference between China and the US.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: it rejects nationalism and the nation-state, so state support for co-ethnics abroad conflicts with its confederal internationalism.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Bookchin treats common resources as belonging to the community, to be managed through municipal assemblies, rather than privately appropriated.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Bookchin values individual freedom within community, but is critical of possessive individualism and bourgeois individualism.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not discussed; municipalizing the economy is the goal, and tax design is not addressed.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: it favours public goods provided through municipal assemblies for all citizens, not means-tested programmes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: Bookchin rejects the parliamentary party and bureaucratic state, preferring assemblies and confederal delegates, but the statement's leader framing is foreign to him.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Bookchin attacks the capitalist market and state; he wants municipal control, so privileges for connected firms are unacceptable.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from his secular, rationalist social ecology, which organises politics through citizens' assemblies, not denominations.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: Bookchin embraces ecological technology and rationalism and rejects tradition-based hierarchy.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Bookchin opposes all hierarchy including patriarchy, and Ocalan's confederalism explicitly stresses women's liberation.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: Bookchin wants resources under municipal control, not national state control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's critique of capitalism and his municipalised, non-private economy; process-only fairness is not discussed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The sources do not mention such a tax; Bookchin opposes both the nation-state and market 'grow-or-die' dynamics, so no clear lean.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's opposition to all hierarchy and his protection of minority rights in assemblies.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's rejection of the state's claim to authority and his ethical case for popular power.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's eco-technology and post-scarcity view of technology freeing people from toil.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's confederation of municipalities in opposition to concentrated power and the nation-state.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Bookchin distanced himself from Marxism's economistic orientation; inferred that he did not rely on labour-value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Bookchin opposes the nation-state and warns that localism can turn parochial or racist, so love of country is not part of the project.

material-over-identity.rationale: Bookchin criticises Marxism's economistic class orientation and holds that all hierarchy, not only class, must be abolished.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Communalism rejects the state, hierarchy and one-party rule and sees markets as a grow-or-die force.

missingStatements.text: Towns and cities should govern themselves through assemblies and link together in confederations, not be subordinate to a national state.
missingStatements.rationale: Municipal confederation replacing the nation-state is the defining institutional proposal of Communalism.

missingStatements.text: The economy should be owned and managed by local communities rather than by private owners or the state.
missingStatements.rationale: Bookchin calls for municipalizing the economy, rejecting both private and nationalized ownership.

notes: Answers rely heavily on inference for topics Bookchin did not discuss. The Rojava (democratic confederalism) variant may differ on identity and religion.
